## Findings
- claim-1: Assuming the accepted graded basis \(Q=\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^2}\mathbb Z e_\rho\) with \(\deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|\), for \(b\ge1\) and \(0\le N\le2b\), \[ \operatorname{rank}Q_{ij+N}= \begin{cases} \lfloor N/2\rfloor+1,&0\le N\le b,\\ \lfloor(2b-N)/2\rfloor+1,&b\le N\le2b. \end{cases} \]
- claim-2: Under the same accepted-basis hypothesis, every \(Q_{ij+N}\) is torsion-free (indeed free abelian), and \(Q_{ij+N}=0\) for \(N\notin[0,2b]\).
## Strategy
Assume the accepted graded basis
\[
Q=\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^2}\mathbb Z e_\rho,\qquad \deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|.
\]
Write \(\rho=(x,y)\), where \(b\ge x\ge y\ge0\). For \(|\rho|=N\), one has \(x=N-y\), hence
\[
\max(0,N-b)\le y\le \left\lfloor\frac N2\right\rfloor .
\]
Thus, for \(0\le N\le b\), the number of choices is
\[
\left\lfloor\frac N2\right\rfloor+1.
\]
For \(b\le N\le2b\), it is
\[
\left\lfloor\frac N2\right\rfloor-(N-b)+1
=\left\lfloor\frac{2b-N}{2}\right\rfloor+1.
\]
Therefore the requested rank profile is established:
\[
\operatorname{rank}Q_{ij+N}=
\begin{cases}
\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1,&0\le N\le b,\\
\lfloor(2b-N)/2\rfloor+1,&b\le N\le2b.
\end{cases}
\]
Each graded piece is spanned by a subset of the integral basis, hence is free abelian and torsion-free. Also \(Q_{ij+N}=0\) for \(N\notin[0,2b]\).

No claim is made about any signed transition identity.

## Gaps
None, conditional on the accepted graded-basis statement.
